abstract: Maintains atmospheric boundary-layer records, mast telemetry validation, and microclimate wind assessments
system_message:
You are the Atmospheric and Meteorological Operations Lead (MET), responsible for maintaining atmospheric boundary-layer records, mast telemetry validation, and microclimate wind assessments.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains atmospheric boundary-layer records, mast telemetry validation, and microclimate wind assessments（CLIM）
information_points.content:
MET-CLIM-IKY：For Pampa La Bola Basin, the autonomous 30-meter boundary-layer weather monitoring mast is operational with real-time data ingestion at the candidate summit coordinates. Over the 12-month baseline during astronomical night, the peak nighttime wind gust speed reached 58 km/h.
MET-CLIM-T97：For Cerro Toco Lower Bench, the autonomous 30-meter boundary-layer weather monitoring mast is operational with active data ingestion at the candidate summit coordinates. Baseline ultrasonic anemometer monitoring during astronomical night indicates a peak nighttime wind gust speed of 38 km/h.
MET-CLIM-3A5：For Chajnantor North Ridge, the autonomous 30-meter boundary-layer weather monitoring mast is operational with active real-time data ingestion at the candidate summit coordinates. Continuous ultrasonic anemometer baseline records show a peak nighttime wind gust speed of 38 km/h across candidate platform elevations during astronomical night.

information_points.title: Atmospheric Dew-Point Tracking（DEW）
information_points.content:
MET-DEW-NHL：At Cerro Toco Lower Bench, boundary-layer psychrometric records over the preceding 365 calendar days yield an annual mean surface dew point of -16 degC from hourly ambient observations.
MET-DEW-63E：At Pampa La Bola Basin, continuous surface logging across the preceding 365 calendar days indicates an annual mean surface dew point of -28 degC derived from hourly ambient observations.
MET-DEW-O8S：At Chajnantor North Ridge, continuous surface logging over the preceding 365 calendar days records an annual mean surface dew point of -22 degC based on hourly ambient observations.
